editorial: When a reckless affair spirals into a serial killer’s vicious rampage, you are thrust into the unsettling world of "Strange Darling," a psychological thriller that refuses to rest. Its unique appeal lies in how it lingers on the shadows of memory, offering an atmosphere that feels both claustrophobic and hypnotically mesmerizing. Joaquin Phoenix delivers a performance of almost no words, each pause a silent gunshot that reverberates long after the credits. The midsection drips with deliberate sluggishness that tests patience, yet the tension never fully abandons you. You’ll find the film’s psychological dread suits those who appreciate a slow-burn thriller that rewards whispered clues over loud twists.
targetAudience: Ideal for fans of psychological thrillers who enjoy non-linear storytelling.
